- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s reversal bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points), especially in early forecast horizon; cap or dampen peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment at end of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
